text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's ruling Socialist Party and its parliamentary allies aprroved the nomination of Interior Minister Nikolay Dobrev as prime minister to replace outgoing Zhan Videnov who resigned at a party congress in December.
-- Bulgaria's December inflation is expected at 27 percent and cumulative inflation for 1996 is seen at 311 percent, experts said.
-- Bulgaria's central bank foreign exchange reserves fell to $518.425 million in December from $525.1 million in November, the Bulgarian National Bank said.
-- Bulgaria expects to receive at least $1 billion proceeds from the privatisation of some 1,000 firms in 1997, the chairman of Privatisation Agency's supervisory board Yosif Iliev said.
-- Bankers from Bulgarian commercial banks put in receivership by the central bank last year might be detained following a prosecutors' meeting due today, Chief Prosecutor's senior official said.
-- Some 80,000 Bulgarians protested in the streets of Sofia against the possible formation of a second socialist cabinet and demanded early parliamentary elections.
-- Bulgaria's exiled king Simeon, currently living in Madrid, is expected to return to his country in the spring, a king's spokeswoman said.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing Socialist cabinet is expected to raise fuel prices by 14-17 percent depending on the grade at its regular meeting today.
-- The leaderships of the Socialist Party and its parliamentary allies are expected to vote on Sunday on a draft list for a new socialist cabinet. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
